events.whyItMatters: First time Apple has committed fab work to Intel Foundry. Signals Intel's foundry turnaround is landing real marquee customers, not just government deals.

phases.headline: Report: Apple in talks with Intel over custom chip manufacturing
Apple and Intel announce multi-year chip manufacturing partnership

events.whyItMatters: Largest buyback authorization in company history. Reads as management signalling the stock is undervalued at current levels despite the run-up.

phases.headline: Nvidia board approves $50B share repurchase program

events.whyItMatters: Would extend AMD's adaptive-computing push beyond the Xilinx deal. Still unconfirmed, so treat as speculative — included because it's already widely reported.

phases.headline: AMD reportedly exploring bid for Lattice Semiconductor

events.whyItMatters: Castlelake's fifth bid was accepted first, but on 2026-07-10 EasyJet's board said it is 'no longer minded to recommend' this £6.90/share (£5.5bn) proposal after Apollo tabled a higher £7.15/share offer. Castlelake still has until Aug 3 to counter, so this is now the trailing bid in a live auction, not the settled outcome.

phases.headline: EasyJet board backs £5.5bn ($7.3bn) take-private proposal from Castlelake

events.whyItMatters: ITV exits broadcasting: selling ITVX and its free-to-air channels to Comcast's Sky for up to £1.6bn leaves ITV a pure-play content producer (ITV Studios) and funds a ~£950m (25p/share) cash return to shareholders. Consolidates UK TV into a Sky-led streaming and advertising champion.

phases.headline: ITV agrees sale of Media & Entertainment arm to Sky for up to £1.6bn

events.whyItMatters: A 20-year lease worth ~$19bn in contracted revenue turns TeraWulf from a bitcoin miner into an AI-infrastructure landlord with two decades of visible revenue — a step-change versus its prior scale. A paired sale of its Abernathy JV stake to Fluidstack (~$450m) funds redeployment into wholly-owned AI capacity.

phases.headline: TeraWulf signs 20-year, ~$19bn AI data-center lease with Anthropic

events.whyItMatters: Buying the Nordics' biggest package-holiday group (Ving, Spies, Tjareborg) turns Norwegian from a point-to-point airline into an end-to-end travel group serving ~30m customers a year, lifting group revenue by close to 50%. The ~SEK 7.94bn price is part-funded with 300m new shares, so holders take dilution now in exchange for vertical integration and a promised 2027 earnings accretion.

phases.headline: Norwegian agrees to acquire Nordic Leisure Travel Group for ~SEK 7.94bn

events.whyItMatters: At EUR 134/share (EUR 3.9bn enterprise value, a 44% premium) Thales buys into surging demand for naval drones used in underwater mine-clearing and anti-submarine warfare, after beating Safran for the asset. It has a binding deal for the Gorge family's 35.5% stake plus a mandatory tender for the rest, so Thales gains critical mass in unmanned mine countermeasures with full control expected by 2028.

phases.headline: Thales agrees EUR 3.9bn deal to acquire control of Exail Technologies

events.whyItMatters: InMode is now the target of a contested take-private: activist holder Steel Partners' $16.75/share all-cash offer (a 20% premium to the unaffected price) tops the CEO-led group's $16.20 bid and lets public holders roll up to 40% into the private company. The board's independent directors must respond by July 13, so the near-term catalyst is whether a bidding war develops or the CEO group prevails.

phases.headline: Steel Partners offers to acquire InMode for $16.75 per share in cash

events.whyItMatters: Prologis's unsolicited ~£12.6bn ($16.9bn) all-share approach for Segro — Europe's largest listed logistics REIT — would consolidate global warehouse ownership under one landlord; Segro's board has rejected it as inadequate and Prologis must table a binding Rule 2.7 offer or walk away by July 22.

phases.headline: Prologis pushes for SEGRO engagement on potential combination

events.whyItMatters: Lockheed's $3.45bn purchase of Ultra Maritime adds sonar, sonobuoy, and torpedo-defense technology to its Rotary and Mission Systems unit, deepening its undersea/anti-submarine-warfare portfolio as allied navies raise maritime-deterrence spending — a bolt-on, not a strategic pivot.

phases.headline: Lockheed to Buy Ultra Maritime for $3.45 Billion in Sea Push

events.whyItMatters: French telecoms investor Xavier Niel becomes Vodafone's largest shareholder, buying e&'s entire 16.2% stake for £4.4bn at a 15% premium — a strong vote of confidence from an experienced sector operator that could pressure management on strategy, though Niel has framed it as a long-term minority holding rather than a takeover approach.

phases.headline: e& Announces USD 5.95 Billion Sale of Vodafone Investment

events.whyItMatters: Equifax's $750m purchase of Mexico's fastest-growing credit bureau (31% YoY revenue growth) gives it a foothold in Latin America's second-largest economy — its 17th bolt-on acquisition in six years, extending a steady inorganic-growth strategy rather than redirecting it.

phases.headline: Equifax Announces Definitive Agreement to Acquire Circulo de Credito in Mexico

events.whyItMatters: Apollo's £7.15/share (£5.7bn/$7.7bn) offer beats Castlelake's accepted £6.90 bid by roughly £1bn and flipped the EasyJet board's recommendation within days of the Castlelake deal being struck, turning what looked like a settled take-private into a live bidding war with the final price and winner both unresolved.

phases.headline: EasyJet board agrees in principle to rival £5.7bn takeover bid from Apollo, topping Castlelake offer

events.whyItMatters: Apple's $30bn+ multiyear commitment to Broadcom is its largest US manufacturing investment to date, locking in onshore supply of custom RF/wireless chips (15bn+ units) and deepening a strategic silicon dependency between the two companies that outlasts any single tariff or trade-policy cycle.

phases.headline: Apple commits $30 billion to Broadcom for U.S. chipmaking push

events.whyItMatters: Kroger's first deal since its $25bn Albertsons merger collapsed in 2024 is a much smaller, lower-risk bolt-on ($1.65bn) that adds ~$9bn of annual sales across five states and signals management is back in dealmaking mode after the antitrust defeat.

phases.headline: Kroger Announces Agreement to Acquire Giant Eagle

events.whyItMatters: Qiagen has drawn early takeover interest from PE firms EQT, Advent, and KKR at prices reportedly above $50/share against a ~$7.85bn market cap, following the company's own retention of Goldman Sachs and Moelis to explore strategic alternatives — still 'early stage' with no assurance of a deal, but it puts a major diagnostics/genomics name in play.

phases.headline: Qiagen Draws Early Takeover Interest From EQT, Advent, KKR

events.whyItMatters: Founder Alice Chang and CyberLink, together holding 81.2% of voting power, sign a binding deal to take Perfect Corp private for $2.00/share cash (a 48% premium), removing the AR/AI beauty-tech name from public markets entirely.

phases.headline: Perfect Corp. Enters into a Definitive Agreement for a Going-Private Transaction

events.whyItMatters: A PE approach values Criteo at roughly $3.7bn, a 50%+ premium, reviving a sale process that stalled in December 2025 — a sign PE still sees value in ad-tech despite the sector's post-cookie malaise. Criteo's board has not yet responded.

phases.headline: Vista Equity, Quinti Capital offer to buy French adtech firm Criteo, sources say

events.whyItMatters: Eni re-enters global commodities trading through a 50/50 JV with Mercuria spanning oil, gas, LNG and biofuels — a strategic pivot to capture the trading profits European peers have booked since the 2022 volatility, pending regulatory approval before launch.

phases.headline: Eni and Mercuria to Establish a Global Trading Joint Venture

events.whyItMatters: Sapporo pays ~$643m for a 25% stake in Carlsberg's new Southeast Asia/Hong Kong venture, handing Carlsberg fresh capital and exclusive regional rights to Sapporo Premium while Sapporo buys distribution scale in a fast-growing beer market it couldn't reach alone.

phases.headline: Carlsberg and Sapporo to form strategic partnership

events.counterparty: Next Geosolutions, WSense, Graal Tech, Defcomm
events.whyItMatters: Fincantieri bundles four bolt-ons (marine survey, underwater comms, AUVs/ASVs) into a vertically-integrated underwater unit already on track for over EUR1.1bn pro forma revenue, joining Thales and Lockheed in the same undersea-defense build-out rather than opportunistic one-off dealmaking.

phases.headline: Fincantieri creates an international underwater champion: acquisition of four companies for an initial expenditure of approximately EUR 600 million
